The Forge is a workshop for offline apps and a tutor for the code underneath them. It opens any single file app, edits every named surface of it live, bakes those edits into a fresh build, ships that build to a Mac, a Windows machine, an iPhone, an iPad or a Fire tablet, and teaches the code behind each thing you do. It can also open itself, edit itself, and bake a new Forge.

The making rooms are the Editor, the Bakery, the Library, Compose and the Workshop. The learning rooms are Magister, the Curriculum, Assessments and Ascensus: three years of code, thirty six modules, seventy two lessons and one hundred and forty four questions, with the first year rendering on the right as you read it. The tools are the Guidebook, Fontes, the Reckoner and Settings. Your own apps, Tabula, Abacus and Scriba, open here as themselves.
An edit is never code. It is one line of data, kept in a
inside the file, which a small reader applies when the page opens: a control hidden, a word changed, an order set, a colour given, a page or a block added. Free

is the one place you write real code, and it is kept only after it parses, fetches nothing, and matches something on the page. The file on the right keeps its own storage behind a shim, so editing a Carpe Diem never touches the Forge, and editing the Forge never touches the copy you are working in.

The Forge is designed and built by Yannie D. Forest, alongside Carpe Diem, as the instrument of doctoral research into whether outsourcing thought to a machine can be reversed. It is built to be calm: one task at a time, folds instead of walls of text, a tip beside the thing it explains, a word on every control, and nothing that scores, streaks or locks you out.

Nothing is fetched from the network, in any room. Nothing you write leaves this device unless you export it yourself. No data you add can run as code. No file is shipped that reports an error when it boots.

The Forge is a workshop for the apps you make and a tutor for the code beneath them. It wears the same four dresses, stands on the same relief, and carries the Carpe Diem seal in its night colours so the two are told apart at a glance.

It does three things. It edits Carpe Diem, live, surface by surface. It bakes your edits into a fresh Carpe Diem file that carries them inside itself. And it keeps what you make, ready to download for any device.
Everything happens on this device. Nothing is fetched. Nothing is sent. There are no streaks, no scores, and nothing that can lock you out.
